title: Block Record
description: The authored definition of one block of work, written at plan time by /plan, /ticket, or /chore. Lives at planning/blocks/<BlockID>.json, one file per block. Governed by D65. Separate from tasks.json, which is the decomposition authored later by /generate-tasks.

id.description: Canonical block ID. Equals the spec directory name exactly, and the basename of this file.

repo.description: Repo slug, as registered in brain.toml.

kind.description: Which producer authored this record and how it is scheduled.

phase.description: Phase number for a roadmap block. Allocated per-repo from state.json, never from a narrative file (D65 section 7). Omit for tickets and chores.

initiative.description: Slug of the owning initiative — the planning/<slug>/ folder holding the authored narrative (plan.md). Omit for standalone tickets and chores.

title.description: Short name. Matches the block's heading in plan.md and the title in state.json.

description.description: One line: what this block is, for a surface that renders more than a title. Never empty — 0 of 894 blocks carried one before D65, and that is the gap this record exists to close.

what.description: The scope, in implementation terms. Concrete enough to decompose into tasks.

why.description: The motivation — why this block, why now in the sequence. Keeps a later decomposition from over- or under-scoping, and is the field whose absence forced intent to be re-derived from diffs.

model.description: Model tier. Rule of thumb: Opus for reasoning/breakdown only; sonnet for high-risk or complex; gemini-pro intermediate; gemini-flash simple.

workflow_rationale.description: Prose explaining the workflow and model choices.

files.description: Files the block touches, named by path. Load-bearing: this is how /generate-tasks derives disjoint task ownership without guessing.

change.description: What changes in the existing file.

interfaces.description: Shared exports, APIs, or contracts the block consumes or must add. Empty array when the project has no shared layer.

out_of_scope.description: Explicit boundaries — what belongs to a later block or a different effort. At least one entry; a block with no stated boundary is under-specified. Note cross-repo or not-yet-built prerequisites here.

acceptance_criteria.description: Each a true/false condition a reviewer can check against the diff, ending with the project's gating checks passing. A criterion whose evidence lives outside this repo's gates must be declared un-gateable per D64.

gateable.description: False when the evidence lives in another process, another repo, a generated artifact, or an installed artefact (D64). A false value requires a named fixture-evidence task.

evidence.description: For an un-gateable criterion: the concrete fixture or command that stands in for the missing gate.

testing_strategy.description: Which test files cover this block and what each must assert. Required in practice for kind=ticket (behaviour-changing work ships with tests); optional for chores.

validation_commands.description: The project's gating commands, from planning/harness.json validation.checks[]. Falls back to that file when omitted.

depends_on.description: Dependency edges, using the same forms as state.json. Mirrored into state.json by the producer until mev derives the scheduling fields from this file (D65 consequences).

oneOf.description: A decision, credential, or judgement call only the operator can supply. Required rather than optional: an operator edge inherits the effective priority of everything it gates and surfaces in /next; the same item written as prose surfaces nowhere.

exit.description: The artifact whose existence ends the gate — never a description of the work.

oneOf.description: A single reducible yes/no on a fixed payload.

carryover_context.description: Slugs of open carryover[] entries this block must not re-break, or that it partly addresses. Loaded from state.json at authoring time — a defect or drift entry touching the same files is either a prerequisite or a constraint.

origin.description: Where this block came from, when it was promoted rather than authored fresh.

forward_looking.description: True for a distant-phase block authored with the full skeleton while context was fresh, whose files and interfaces are provisional and expected to be refined when it becomes next.

spec_dir.description: Repo-relative path to the spec directory. Equals planning/<id>/ exactly, no title suffix (D65 section 3).

related.description: OKF doc_ids this block relates to. At least one real doc_id keeps it off the isolated-node warning; never invent one.

notes.description: Constraints, follow-ups, or known edge cases not covered by this block.

created.description: Authoring date. Bare vocabulary matching carryover[] and backlog[], not created_at (D65 section 10).

updated.description: Date this definition was last revised — the signal that a forward-looking block was refined when it became next.

closed.description: Date the block closed. Mirrors the state.json tombstone.

commit.description: Git hash of the closing commit, for fast later retrieval. Mirrors the state.json tombstone.
